title: Building a community
hook: The first thing he built was a masjid. The second was a brotherhood.

screens.text: **The first thing he built in Madinah was a masjid.** The second wasn't a building at all. It was a brotherhood, and it's the reason your masjid gives you a mentor.

**A simple masjid.** On a plot of land where his camel had knelt, they built a masjid of palm trunks with a roof of palm leaves. The Companions carried the stones, and the Prophet ﷺ was right there with them [Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: One report says the plot was a date yard belonging to two orphans; another says the clan who owned it refused any payment [Bukhari 3906; Bukhari 428].

screens.text: Tap around a masjid. The first one in Madinah was much simpler, but the purpose is the same.

areas.entrance: Where newcomers walk in. In Madinah, newcomers from Makkah were each given a local brother [IslamQA 11575].
areas.hall: Where people pray in rows. The first hall had palm-trunk pillars and a palm-leaf roof [IslamQA 11575].
areas.wudu: Where you wash before prayer, like you learned in Day 2.
areas.minbar: Where the Friday talk is given. Today's masjid is still the community's meeting place.

screens.text: **Brothers by choice.** The people arriving from Makkah had left homes, jobs and family behind. So he paired each newcomer with a host from Madinah, as brothers [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta 733].
bubbles: The newcomers became known as the Muhajirun, "those who emigrated". Their hosts were the Ansar, "the helpers".

cards.back: Offered his new brother half of everything he owned [Bukhari 2048].
Thanked him, and asked only: where's the market? [Bukhari 2048]
He started trading and stood on his own feet. Generosity met dignity [Bukhari 2048].

screens.text: **A city with many groups.** Madinah also had Jewish tribes and others. He set out an agreement with them for defending the city together and for each group's religious freedom [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (Medina)].
bubbles: He found Madinah's Jews fasting on 'Ashura to remember Musa (Moses). He said Muslims had even more right to Musa, and fasted it too [Bukhari 2004].

screens.text: How a town became a community.

events.title: A masjid
events.text: Built simply, with the Prophet ﷺ working alongside everyone [Bukhari 428].

events.title: A brotherhood
events.text: Each newcomer paired with a local brother [IslamQA 11575].

events.title: An agreement
events.text: Madinah's groups agree to defend the city together [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (Medina)].

events.title: 'Ashura
events.text: He fasts the day Allah saved Musa [Bukhari 2004].

screens.text: **A masjid is meant to be a family.** The brotherhood is the model for mentoring a new Muslim. If your masjid has given you a mentor, that's this sunnah. And one day, you might be the Sa'd for someone else.
bubbles: 'Ashura and the Muslim year were covered in Day 79. Praying in rows together was Day 22.

screens.situation: Keisha has been Muslim a year. A new convert, Ana, just lost her job and her family isn't speaking to her. Keisha wants to help but isn't rich.

options.text: Offer what she can: time, a meal, help with job applications, and introductions
options.feedback: Yes. Brotherhood and sisterhood is practical. Sa'd offered what he had; Keisha can too.

options.text: Leave it to the masjid office; she's not qualified
options.feedback: Not quite. The masjid can help too, but the Madinah model was person to person.

options.text: Hand her a big check she can't afford
options.feedback: Not quite. Help shouldn't break her. A meal, a ride or her network can matter as much.

screens.text: He built a masjid, then built people into a family. That's what a masjid is for, and you belong in it.
Next episode: a call to prayer seen in a dream, and a direction that changed in the middle of a prayer.

check.prompt: What did 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf ask his new brother for?

options.feedback: Right. He thanked Sa'd for his offer of half his wealth and went to earn his own living.
Not quite. That was Sa'd's offer. 'Abd al-Rahman thanked him and asked only for the market.

check.prompt: How was the first masjid in Madinah built?

options.text: Simply, from palm trunks and leaves, with the Prophet ﷺ working alongside
options.feedback: Right. Simple materials, and everyone carried stones together.
Not quite. It was simple: palm trunks and leaves, built by the community.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The masjid was built where the camel knelt. Bukhari 3906: a date-drying yard of two orphans, Sahl and Suhayl. Bukhari 428: Banu al-Najjar refused payment. Give both briefly, or say "a plot of land". It was simple: palm trunks and palm-leaf roofing; the Companions carried stones and he was with them [Bukhari 428; IslamQA 11575].
- He paired each emigrant from Makkah (the Muhajirun) with a host from Madinah (the Ansar) as brothers [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta Egypt (Coexistence in Medina)].
- Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' offered half his wealth to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who thanked him and asked to be shown the market [Bukhari 2048].
- He set out an agreement with Madinah's groups, including its Jewish tribes, for mutual defence and religious freedom [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen (The Constitution of Medina); Dar al-Ifta Egypt (Coexistence in Medina)].
- He found the Jews of Madinah fasting 'Ashura for Musa, said Muslims have more right to Musa, and fasted it [Bukhari 2004]; Day 79 covers 'Ashura.

**Likely questions**
- *"Was it the world's first constitution?"* Say "an agreement". Scholars agree agreements were made, but no sound chain exists for the full text as one document [Yaqeen (The Constitution of Medina)]. Don't quote clauses or make "first constitution" claims.
- *"Who were the Ansar and the Muhajirun?"* The emigrants from Makkah and the helpers of Madinah, paired as brothers.
- *"Why do Muslims fast on 'Ashura?"* Point to Day 79 [Bukhari 2004].
- *"How do I find a mentor?"* Point to their masjid's mentor programme in the app and the imam.

**Escalate:** nothing specific.

**Don't**
- Don't call the Madinah agreement "the world's first constitution" or quote its clauses.
- Don't use this episode to make claims about Jews today; keep to the agreement and 'Ashura as told.

- [Bukhari 2048](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2048) (Sahih): Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf.
